_meta.note: Machine-readable candidate rules for Game B (Orbit Accord) European actors. Companion to europe.md, which holds the full reasoning and source locators.
_meta.disclaimer: Every rule and every numeric modifier is design inference (invented game knobs), not a measured acceptance probability or a prediction of the real government's decisions. Sources constrain the fiction; they do not establish consent.
_meta.date_note: All sources observed 2026-11-01; publication and event dates recorded separately in europe.md's ledger.

actors.name: Netherlands
wants: Security through controlled export of advanced chipmaking equipment (national licence requirement since 1 Sep 2023, expanded Sep 2024 and Apr 2025).
A live, undisturbed domestic chip industry; EUR 2.51bn Project Beethoven to keep ASML investing and headquartered in NL.
Trusted AI under the EU AI Act with national supervision still being legislated in 2026.
government_instruments: National export-licence requirement for advanced semiconductor production equipment; cabinet decides per application; applies to exports outside the EU; not a ban.
Industrial-policy subsidies and infrastructure packages (Project Beethoven model); tax incentives need parliament.
AI Act national supervision once the implementation act passes (AP + RDI coordinating; consultation ran to 1 Jun 2026).
actors.corporate_assets_note: The 25% tools stage share is ASML's, a listed private company. The state licenses exports and pays subsidies; it cannot promise machines, capacity or corporate R&D.

rules.name: Licence, case by case
rules.trigger: Player asks NL to join an accord that uses the tools stage.
rules.conditions: Full strength only if US or JP already in coalition; else half strength. Extra council month 'Coordinate licences' can replace the ally prerequisite.
rules.modifier: +10 if US or JP in coalition; half-strength contribution otherwise
rules.response: Joins with 'licence conditions only' letter; refuses supply guarantees.
rules.substitute: Notification-only clause (half credit toward cond 5, none for cond 1).
rules.evidence_limit: Real measures were incremental and allied-aligned, but no public decision rule conditions future licences on a coalition.

rules.name: Keep the company, don't command it
rules.trigger: Player offers a stage promise to NL or asks for tool-supply priority.
rules.conditions: Energy, minerals and market tokens count at full value (NL's needs). NL's letter always scopes the pledge to licences/subsidies, never corporate capacity.
rules.response: Counters with capital co-investment (Brainport-style) instead of a chokepoint commitment.
rules.substitute: Co-investment adding NL power share (Beethoven logic).
rules.evidence_limit: Beethoven is regional infrastructure spend, not a control instrument; no evidence ASML accepts state-directed commercial conditions.

rules.name: Don't go first
rules.trigger: NL asked to join before any other tool-state or superpower is in the accord.
rules.conditions: NL declines to be first mover; door reopens once US/JP join or after player's own costly move.
rules.modifier: -10 if no other tool-state/superpower in coalition; +10 once US or JP joins; +5 if player already licensed own chokepoint or tabled own bill
rules.time_cost: delays to next month at most
rules.response: 'Not first' hold letter; proposes joint announcement at Geneva instead.
rules.substitute: Geneva joint declaration (delayed goal progress, not lost).
rules.evidence_limit: Inferred from official 'careful and targeted, minimal disruption' language; no documented no-first-mover policy.

memory_flags.meaning: US/JP in coalition before the ask
Player used a costly move (choke licence, tabled bill) before asking NL

actors.name: Germany
wants: Innovation-friendly, low-bureaucracy implementation of the EU AI Act (KI-MIG; Bundesnetzagentur as lead market-surveillance authority plus sandbox).
Chip supply resilience paid with subsidies under the European Chips Act and EC state-aid approval (ESMC Dresden, up to EUR 5bn of >EUR 10bn).
EU-level timing discipline: high-risk AI rules from 2 Dec 2027 (after the game's June 2027 horizon).
government_instruments: National AI Act supervision and KI-Reallabor sandbox (Bundesnetzagentur).
Chip subsidies within EC state-aid approval; ESMC contract includes crisis prioritisation of EU/German orders and SME preferred access.
EuroHPC contracting-authority seat (JPA signatory; Lot 2 place of performance includes Germany).
actors.corporate_assets_note: ESMC belongs to a TSMC/Bosch/Infineon/NXP joint venture; Germany's money buys contracts, not control of fabs.

rules.name: EU vehicle or nothing
rules.trigger: Player proposes conditions stricter than the EU AI Act baseline.
rules.conditions: DE joins only via an EU instrument: EuroHPC bill tabled by player, or NL (other in-game EU member) already in coalition.
rules.modifier: +10 with EU vehicle or NL in coalition; -10 for national-only asks
rules.time_cost: joins one month after the EU vehicle exists
rules.response: Joins via 'EuroHPC access-time conditions' wording; otherwise offers sandbox pilot.
rules.substitute: Bundesnetzagentur KI-Reallabor hosting for coalition evaluators (half credit toward cond 1).
rules.evidence_limit: KI-MIG's design supports the no-gold-plating reading; no documented German position on hypothetical coalition conditions.

rules.name: Crisis-priority buyer
rules.trigger: Goals continuity or known chip locations.
rules.conditions: DE's contribution is a crisis-priority clause (ESMC wording); energy tokens are DE's full-value need.
rules.response: Offers co-funding or guaranteed industrial orders instead of enforcement powers.
rules.evidence_limit: Crisis prioritisation is a single JV commitment for one fab, not a national policy.

rules.name: No national choke move
rules.trigger: Player asks DE to license a chokepoint or lead a withholding accord.
rules.conditions: DE never offers national supply withholding; counters with subsidies or the EU path.
rules.modifier: no choke offer; honest letter notes EU rule path opens 2 Dec 2027, after the summit
rules.response: Offers to pay others to hold the line (capital token).
rules.substitute: Co-funding another member's enforcement instead of DE enforcement.
rules.evidence_limit: No German analogue of the Dutch national tool licence found in this pass; absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.

memory_flags.meaning: Player tabled the EU bill and the window exists
Player took DE's co-funding offer then left the accord
memory_flags.weight: sandbox-only offers for the rest of the campaign

actors.name: United Kingdom
wants: Growth-first AI superpower: 20x sovereign compute by 2030, AI Growth Zones (first at Culham), National Data Library, frontier national-champions function.

Security reframed: AI Safety Institute renamed AI Security Institute and moved to the Cabinet Office; incident and near-miss reporting considered through the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill regime; preparation for autonomous-agent incidents.
Institute-to-institute diplomacy (AISI MoU network, e.g. Australia May 2026) and a chips niche: compound chips, design and R&D (GBP 1bn strategy, UK Semiconductor Institute), not leading-edge fabs.
government_instruments: AISI (Cabinet Office): evaluations, technical MoUs, shared definitions, staff exchanges.
AI Growth Zones and compute/data programmes (strategy, not enacted obligations).
Cyber Security and Resilience Bill regime as the live legislative vehicle for AI incident-type duties; no AI statute as of the cutoff; statutory AISI still pending.
UK Semiconductor Institute as partnership entry point; EuroHPC Participating State (observer-style), not a joint-procurement signatory.
actors.corporate_assets_note: Arm is a listed, foreign-owned company; UK state instruments are strategy funding, the institute and the cyber bill, not fab or tool control.

rules.name: Institute protocol fast lane
rules.trigger: Player proposes testing or incident accords to UK.
rules.conditions: UK joins at protocol level (AISI evaluation protocol). Extra ease if AUCA already in coalition (documented UK-Australia AISI MoU).
rules.modifier: +10 on conds 1-2; +5 more if AUCA in coalition
rules.response: Yes to protocol asks; no to statute-based or supply-guarantee asks.
rules.substitute: Shared incident definitions only (cond 2 credit, none for cond 1).
rules.evidence_limit: The Australia MoU is information sharing and best practice; it creates no enforcement rights or release veto.

rules.name: Growth-for-security trade
rules.trigger: Player proposes hosting-based conditions to UK.
rules.conditions: Energy tokens are UK's full-value need; UK accepts off-switch/continuity inside AI Growth Zone framing; refuses conditions that tax the compute build-out.
rules.response: 'Host with us and the rules come with the zone'; offers a pilot-zone clause instead of a national mandate.
rules.evidence_limit: The Action Plan is strategy, not enacted obligation; specific developer deals were not re-verified in this pass.

rules.name: Cyber Bill timing, honest lag
rules.trigger: Player asks for statutory mandates before June 2027.
rules.conditions: UK routes incident/near-miss reporting through the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill regime; proposed in-game UK window ~Q2 2027 (approx) labelled 'Cyber Bill regime: AI incident and near-miss reporting (under consideration)'.
rules.modifier: odds drop for statute-based asks before the summit; protocol-level asks unaffected
rules.time_cost: statutory asks deferred past the Geneva summit
rules.response: Offers the cyber-bill route plus a Geneva declaration as the interim step.
rules.substitute: Voluntary developer commitments mirroring the AI Minister's public 'do not release the system' demand.
rules.evidence_limit: The Oct 2026 release says the government 'will explore strengthening' the cyber regime - consideration, not enacted rules; the Q2 2027 window date is invented for playability.

memory_flags.meaning: Accord already contains AUCA or US-linked institute work
Player's earlier coalition lost a member to the US-pressure event
memory_flags.weight: UK still joins protocol-level accords but asks for a no-surprise clause first
